alerts.name: Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
alerts.desc: The response does not include the X-Frame-Options header. The page may be embedded inside an iframe on an attacker-controlled site, enabling clickjacking.
alerts.solution: Add a X-Frame-Options header with value DENY or SAMEORIGIN, or a suitable frame-ancestors CSP directive.

instances.evidence: X-Frame-Options header was not present in the response
X-Frame-Options header was not present in the response

alerts.name: X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
alerts.desc: The response does not set the X-Content-Type-Options header, so browsers may MIME-sniff the response away from the declared content type.

alerts.alert: Content Security Policy Header Not Set
alerts.name: Content Security Policy Header Not Set
alerts.desc: Content Security Policy (CSP) header not set. Without CSP the browser has no allowlist for scripts, styles and other resources.
alerts.solution: Deploy a CSP header compatible with the page's scripts and resources; do not blindly use default-src 'none' if it breaks the application.

alerts.name: Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
alerts.desc: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) header is not set. Note that HSTS only applies to HTTPS responses.
alerts.solution: Once the site is served over HTTPS, add a Strict-Transport-Security header with an appropriate max-age.

alerts.name: Server Banner Disclosure
alerts.desc: The response discloses the server product or version in a header or error page.
alerts.solution: Remove or minimize version banners in production responses.
